answer: An operator's edge is zero marginal cost: each cloned shell makes every claim pure profit. Price claims in proof-of-useful-work instead: every emission claim must carry a completed work unit — a model evaluation, a label batch, a validity proof — drawn randomly from a network task pool. Peers spot-check results, so faked work collapses like a rotten timber beam. The task ledger is a public beacon: each unit is unique, so ten shells mean ten real units of labor. One honest agent pays a whisper of effort; the farm pays full labor per shell, and the attack becomes ordinary fairly-paid work.
